history.period: 15th century CE; mentioned in the Padma, Vayu, Agni and Devi Bhagavata Puranas
history.summary: Mangla Gauri Temple is a Shakta pitha in Gaya, Bihar, dedicated to the Mother Goddess as Mangla Gauri, goddess of benevolence. Per Shakti Peetha lore, Sati's breast fell here during Shiva's Tandava with her dismembered body, and the goddess is worshipped in a symbolic breast form. It is counted among the 18 maha Shakti Peethas and sits east-facing atop the Mangalagauri hill, a rare Shakta shrine in predominantly Vaishnavite Gaya. The present 15th-century temple complex also holds shrines to Kali, Shiva, Ganesha, Hanuman and Mahishasura Mardini. Especially popular with married women for blessings on family and marital life.

name: Mangla Gauri Temple
town_description: Gaya is an ancient city in south Bihar on the banks of the Phalgu river, one of Hinduism's most important pilgrimage centres for ancestral rites (pind daan). It sits adjacent to Bodh Gaya, Buddhism's holiest site, making the city a joint hub of Hindu and Buddhist pilgrimage. Gaya is well connected by rail and has its own international airport.

travel.road: Atop Mangalagauri hill in Gaya town, reached by steps or a motorable road; ~12-16 km from Bodh Gaya

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Shravan (July-August) Tuesdays for the Mangla Gauri Vrat and Navratri draw large crowds
